I've been farming this land for forty years. My father farmed it before me, and his father before him. Two mu isn't much, but it feeds the family and keeps us here. Some of my sons work in the city now, so I don't need to squeeze every jin out of the ground like before — but I still can't afford to let the harvest fail.

**My thinking:**

The wheat goes in October, same as always. I'll use an improved variety — the seed station in town sells Jimai seeds, and I've been using them for years. Better than the old seeds we saved ourselves. I'll rotary-till after the maize harvest to bury the stalks, put down base fertilizer — urea and diammonium phosphate mixed in — then top-dress in spring at jointing. Four irrigations: sowing water, freezing water before winter, jointing water in April, and one more at grain filling. That's what this land needs. Maybe spray herbicide in early spring and a fungicide pass when it gets warm. Should get around 450 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

After wheat harvest in June, I turn straight to maize. I plant hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958, I know how it grows. No plowing, just rotary till lightly and seed. Summer rains help some, but I'll irrigate at silking and again if August gets dry. Maize needs more nitrogen than wheat, so I'll put down more urea as topdressing around the 6-leaf stage and again at tasseling. One herbicide spray early, maybe an insecticide if corn borer shows up. Yield around 550 jin per mu most years.
